requirement_text.REQ-124: MOB-2 (docs/mobile/requirements.md) needs GET /tenant-config to return { realm_url, locales, default_locale, branding, environment_kind } WITHOUT a bearer token: the mobile app calls it to discover which realm to authenticate against, so by definition it has no token yet. Verified against lib/ on 2026-08-21, this is two gaps, not one: (a) Letflow.Routers.TenantConfig is a stub whose routes land in REQ-078; and (b) Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline mounts it behind Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, so implementing the route is not sufficient -- it would still demand the token the caller cannot have. Resolve (b) explicitly: either an unauthenticated variant mounted ahead of AuthPipeline, or a documented exemption inside it. Pick one and record why in the moduledoc. This is the gate for the entire mobile tier -- without it the app cannot reach a login screen -- which is why it is sequenced first in docs/mobile/build-order.md phase M-0. Security scope: an unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data is a tenant-data path by definition and needs SECURITY-REVIEWER. The response must expose only what bootstrap requires. Check the shape field-by-field against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md -- in particular whether an unauthenticated caller enumerating slugs can learn which tenants exist, and what the answer should be for a slug that does not exist.

task.description: This diff is explicitly in scope -- do not stop at the scope test. Run: git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/routers/mobile_tenant_config.ex lib/letflow/router.ex, then determine APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE for each of INV-1..INV-8 against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md, and for each APPLIES invariant run its 'How to verify' check against the actual diff -- not against the design doc's claims. Give explicit, first-hand attention to: (1) INV-2 (response-shaping allowlist) -- confirm mobile_config_map/1 is a hand-built map literal with exactly 5 keys and is never derived from %Letflow.Identity.Tenant{} or Map.from_struct/1, by reading the actual function body. (2) INV-5-flavored tenant-enumeration risk on an unauthenticated per-tenant-data endpoint -- confirm every branch (resolvable slug, unknown slug, missing slug, DB error/exception) produces a byte-identical response for the four non-realm_url fields, and that realm_url's variance is the minimum necessary disclosure (same class of information any authenticated user of that tenant already has), not an unjustified expansion. (3) INV-4 -- confirm no exception is logged (only the caller-supplied slug), and no secret material (env-sourced or otherwise) appears in the response or logs. (4) Confirm this route is mounted ONLY on Letflow.Router, never inside Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline, so the exemption from Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline is structurally scoped to this one route and /api/tenant-config -- not pipeline-wide -- by reading the actual diff to Letflow.Router and confirming zero lines changed in api_pipeline.ex/auth_pipeline.ex (git diff --stat already shows this from Step 2a; verify it yourself, don't take Step 2a's word for it).
acceptance_criteria: Scope test result stated (in scope -- unauthenticated endpoint returning per-tenant data)
Every applicable invariant (expect at minimum INV-2, INV-4, INV-5-flavored) verdicted PASS/FAIL against the actual code, not the design doc
Tenant-enumeration risk explicitly assessed: what an attacker with a slug wordlist can and cannot learn from this endpoint
Unknown-slug behavior explicitly confirmed as byte-identical to the default/miss/error branches
Confirmation that the AuthPipeline exemption is route-scoped, not pipeline-wide
